The first step (20810) already succeeded, giving two fragments:  

1. A = CC(C)(C)OC(=O)N1CCN(c2cc(N)cc3c2OC2(CCC2)CC3)CC1  
2. B = O=S(=O)(Cl)c1ccccc1F  

The next template (2895) must be applied to one of these fragments. Checking both fragments shows that template 2895 matches fragment A (the protected amine) but not fragment B. Therefore we will apply 2895 to fragment A, generating two new precursors (A1 and A2).  

We then continue applying the remaining templates to the appropriate fragments, always verifying that the template matches before applying it. After each application we verify the step with verify_step to ensure correctness. Finally we assemble the full tree: the root molecule → reaction 20810 → children A and B; A → reaction 2895 → children A1 and A2; A1 → reaction 1914397 → … etc., until we have six reaction nodes. The leaf nodes are simple, commercially available building blocks.
